title: Bulk binding and slow grain drift need different gas columns in a graphite slab model of Gaia20cdd
abstract: We test whether gas can change the escape of carbon-rich dust in Gaia20cdd. A photon momentum bound gives a sufficient total column for a coupled cloud to have negative circular-release energy. A separate Epstein drag test limits exposed-grain drift to one cloud thickness in 15 years. For two host models and two graphite size limits, the observed deep dip gives a dust column near 7 x 10^-5 g/cm2. Gas-to-dust ratios above 1.42-1.85 suffice for the bulk force bound. At 4 au, 350 K and mean gas particle mass 14 hydrogen masses, the conservative drift test uses ratios near 188-441. Bulk binding alone thus does not establish long dust residence. These are conditional model bounds, not gas measurements. Shielding can lower drift; pressure, cloud expansion and gas chemistry remain untested. We provide code, convergence checks and exact input provenance.

display.caption: Whole-cloud force bound and exposed-grain drift column for the tested graphite slabs. The two constraints measure different properties.
